![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072211/assets/dc432b01077dc153940a88689f398283c09ee2a9d3385f4619a2e4a12cfa9c10.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 4-x-y},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072211/assets/fcb2a304b7333a8ee3d2ae38c26b337fa4e486f0d33034b68982dc9f2cc0bb11.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 4-x-y}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4-x-y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(4-x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[(4-x)y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((4-x)-\frac{1}{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{7}{2}-x)\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{7x}{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
